body: Putting _ctx.download_and_extract_ at the end of function __http_archive_impl_ seems to fix the multiple downloads. Not sure why....

Manged to reproduce the issue; thanks a lot for the detailed
reproduction case!

The underlying issue seems to be the implicit restart in the
evaluation of skylark code; the HttpDownloader gets called several
times. As a workaround, while I'm working on a proper solution,
I can offer the use of `--experimental_repository_cache` which
will ensure that the second and third download is at least taken
from local disk, so the network is accessed only once. I hope,
we can get that feature out of experimental soon (as it will also
help with several independent projects sharing a common dependency).

--

ada0c370c2a3ea484925bc4e7d927b015bc4ad92 makes `http_archive` work well with the current restart semantics: it makes sure, we reference everything we need later before calling out to the network the first time.

However, there is an ongoing design discussion about changing the current semantics to something that makes it easier to write correct repository rules. So I leave the issue open as a placeholder of how the repository rules should work to avoid unnecessary (and, in particular, duplicate) network access.

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
Current behavior of repository rules, documented here: https://docs.bazel.build/versions/master/skylark/repository_rules.html#when-is-the-implementation-function-executed:

> The implementation function can be restarted if a dependency it request is missing. The beginning of the implementation function will be re-executed after the dependency has been resolved.

causes pretty bad unexpected behaviors, evidenced, for example, in this patch: https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/commit/ada0c370c2a3ea484925bc4e7d927b015bc4ad92

We must make sure that repository rule functions **never _observably_ re-execute**. Otherwise the semantics of repository rules is magic, extremely hard to debug and reason about. It pains me greatly that we are shipping something this broken. 

One potential way to fix it is to implement restarts from arbitrary execution point in Skylark interpreter (continuation save/restore).

body: As ada0c37 fixes the immediate issue, closing this. #4533 tracks the larger issue (technically classified as feature request, as current behavior is actually docoemented and WAI, although I do view this as a design bug)

issue.body:
Commit bd16ab9454e624a26c53a0f3fb892e20fb1c36e6 documents that these statements are no longer required to achieve prefetching (as of commit cdc99afc1a03ff8fbbbae088d358b7c029e0d232).  Given that many `http_archive` calls will need at least a `build_file`, these debugging prints generate an incredible amount of spam in projects with many external archives.

I looked over the rest of the `build_defs/repo` files and none of them have any tracing debug prints, except for `git.bzl` which guards it with an `attr.verbose`.  I could rework this to add a verbosity flag if you wish, but it doesn't seem merited for http fetching (unlike git, which is relatively more expensive and can be flaky).

Relates to #2700.
